edges.effect_quant: In the Mi-Iron randomized trial of 104 adults with HFE-related hemochromatosis and moderate iron overload, iron-reduction treatment improved fatigue scores versus sham by 6.3 points on the Modified Fatigue Impact Scale; in a biopsy series of treated C282Y homozygotes, fibrosis regressed by at least two METAVIR stages in 69% of F3 and 35% of F4 cases.
edges.population: adults with HFE-related hereditary hemochromatosis receiving therapeutic venesection or erythrocytapheresis
edges.mechanism: Repeated phlebotomy removes iron-containing erythrocytes, progressively reducing ferritin, transferrin saturation, and tissue iron deposition. Lower iron burden can then relieve oxidative injury and allow partial recovery in organs such as liver and heart when treatment begins before irreversible damage is complete.
edges.summary: Therapeutic phlebotomy is one of the clearest disease-modifying interventions in hemochromatosis, with evidence of improved symptoms and regression of some organ injury as iron stores are normalized. The magnitude of benefit depends on how early treatment starts, but the direction is consistently favorable.
edges.caveats: Not every manifestation is fully reversible, especially advanced cirrhosis, arthropathy, or long-standing endocrine injury. Most evidence is from relatively small cohorts or surrogate-organ studies, although the randomized Mi-Iron trial strengthens the causal case for benefit in moderate overload.

evidence.notes: Reversibility of hepatic fibrosis in treated genetic hemochromatosis: a study of 36 cases.
